document.abstract: Both theater projection of color films and color television transmission of color films place certain limits on the variation of color and density balance between reels of a feature presentation or between the different intercut materials which make up a complete television show. While these limits may be the same in both cases, the problem of achieving such control is much more apparent in color television because of the nature of television programing.
